# Horizontal treadle loom (`treadle_loom`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/manufacturing.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Tools, machines & manufacturing (`manufacturing`)
- Deps: needs textile_fibres; helped by spinning_wheel
- Core idea: Cloth is made by passing a weft thread across between two sets of stretched warp threads and then exchanging the sets. On the treadle loom the warp runs horizontally from a warp beam to a cloth beam, so cloth of any length can be wound on. Each warp thread passes through an eye in a heddle; the heddles hang on two or more shafts joined to foot treadles, so pressing a treadle raises one set of threads and lowers the other. The hands are free to throw the shuttle through the opening and to pull the reed, a hanging comb that keeps the threads evenly spaced and beats each weft against the cloth. It weaves several times faster than the upright looms it replaced; more shafts give twills and patterns.
- Pitfalls:
  - Uneven warp tension, which gives baggy stripes and broken threads
  - No reed, so the cloth narrows and the edges pull in
  - Unsized, fuzzy warp yarn that chafes through in the heddles
- History: egypt: c. 4400 BC – horizontal ground loom pictured on a dish from Badari (no treadles); china: c. 2nd c. BC – pattern loom models in a tomb at Laoguanshan, Chengdu; 1st–2nd c. AD treadle looms on Han stone reliefs; india: pit treadle loom for cotton; date of origin uncertain, well established by the medieval period; islamic: early medieval – treadle and draw looms for silk across Iran, Syria and Spain; africa: c. 11th c. – narrow-strip treadle weaving in West Africa (Tellem textiles, Mali); americas: pre-Columbian – backstrap and staked looms without treadles; the treadle loom arrives with the Spanish; europe: 10th–11th c. – horizontal treadle loom replaces the warp-weighted loom in towns; broadloom for two weavers in the 13th c.
- Read:
  - Eric Broudy, The Book of Looms: A History of the Handloom from Ancient Times to the Present (1979)
  - Feng Zhao et al., The earliest evidence of pattern looms: Han Dynasty tomb models from Chengdu, China, Antiquity 91 (2017)
